Day 20 of 100 · AWS Networking Foundations

AWS Systems Manager

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityAWS Networking FoundationsTopic verified by artifact

Systems Manager provides managed operational channels for instances and nodes so administration does not have to revolve around exposed SSH access.

Architecture / mental model

Operator / automation → Systems Manager service → managed node via agent + IAM

How it works

Systems Manager includes capabilities such as Session Manager, Run Command, inventory and patch operations. Managed nodes need the right agent/connectivity and IAM permissions.

Session Manager can remove the need to expose inbound SSH for routine administration. Access can instead be governed by IAM and recorded through the Systems Manager control plane.

The operational win is consistency: commands and maintenance actions can target managed fleets instead of relying on somebody remembering which host needs a manual login.

Hands-on reference

aws ssm describe-instance-information
aws ssm start-session --target INSTANCE_ID

Verification

Confirm the node appears as managed, then open a Session Manager session or run a harmless command and verify the result/audit trail.

Field note / gotcha

Closing port 22 does not magically make Session Manager work. Agent health, network access to SSM endpoints and the instance role all have to be correct.

Security considerations

Scope who can start sessions/run commands, log administrative activity and avoid giving the managed-node role unrelated permissions.

What I learned

Remote administration is stronger when access is an authenticated control-plane action rather than a permanently exposed network service.
